title: CompTIA legal, trademark, and content-IP hardening

preflight.note: Created from a repository-specific CompTIA legal/IP risk review before cleanup implementation begins.

acceptance_criteria.text: Inventory every current consumer-facing and authoring surface that references CompTIA, A+, Network+, Security+, exam identifiers, exam objectives, passing scores, affiliation/endorsement, or legacy Apex A+ Academy branding, and record the exact files/surfaces that require change or explicit no-action disposition.

Replace verbatim or substantially verbatim CompTIA objective-title text in the A+, Network+, and Security+ objective registries with original SkillForge-authored summaries while preserving objective codes, exam mappings, domains, IDs, ordering, and objective coverage; validate that lessons/questions/PBQs/flashcards continue to resolve to the same objectives.

Remove claims that SkillForge raw mock-exam percentages are CompTIA's official passing line or are direct conversions of CompTIA scaled scores. Model and label SkillForge readiness benchmarks as SkillForge-owned practice heuristics, retain official CompTIA scaled-score facts only where accurately sourced, and ensure A+ Core 1/Core 2 are not collapsed into a misleading single official percentage.

Audit trademark presentation across README, application UI, manifests, installer/release copy, screenshots/store-facing metadata, and documentation so SkillForge remains the primary product brand; retain clear non-affiliation/non-endorsement language; and remove or explicitly prohibit unlicensed CompTIA logos, certification badges, partner marks, or 'official/authorized' claims.

Add or update a durable third-party trademark/IP notice explaining that CompTIA and its certification marks belong to CompTIA, that SkillForge is independent, and that the repository's Apache-2.0 license does not grant rights to third-party trademarks or proprietary third-party assessment material.

Audit legacy 'Apex A+ Academy' consumer-facing references and historical release surfaces, retire or clearly contextualize legacy branding where it could imply that A+ is part of the product's own mark, and preserve legacy application IDs/storage keys/backup extensions only where required for backward compatibility with that rationale documented.

Strengthen content-provenance governance so contributors and maintainers must author original educational material from public objectives, standards, documentation, and subject-matter knowledge; must not submit recalled live exam questions, dumps, reconstructed PBQs, or proprietary assessment content; and must record a review of the existing A+/Network+/Security+ banks against that rule.

Publish a closeout audit summarizing the legal/IP hardening changes, residual risks that require qualified counsel or an actual CompTIA license/partner agreement, and evidence from repository validation/tests showing the cleanup did not reduce objective coverage or break certification-track behavior.

source: Repository-specific CompTIA legal/IP risk review requested by the Steward on 2026-08-08
